subject: Graph contains a cycle - using latent to select covariate value?

messages.author: 6fee017125c7bf75
messages.subject: Graph contains a cycle - using latent to select covariate value?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to run an RSF where my latent variable is used to select the covariate grid location/value. I'm getting the error that my graph contains a cycle - which it does. I can't quite logic my way out of this and hoping for some help.

I've pulled apart the variables into lat and lon because I was trying to debug dimension issues - will loop in the end. 

Here is code with an example that reproduces the error:

nearest <- nimbleFunction(
run = function(x1 = double(1), #double(1) is vector of numeric values of unknown size
x2 = double(1),
y1 = double(1),
y2 = double(1)) {
dist <- numeric(length(y2))
for(i in 1:length(y2)) {
dist[i] <- sqrt(((x1 - y1[i]) ^2) + ((x2 - y2[i]) ^2))[1] }
id <- which(dist == min(dist))
return(id)
returnType(integer(0)) #double(0) should also work
}
)

#---- hab model ----
#s is observed data 
#mu is latent state (real locations)
postModelCode <- nimbleCode({
#priors
beta1 ~ dmnorm(0, 10)
psi_lat ~ dt(mu = 0, tau = 1, df = 3)
psi_lon ~ dt(mu = 0, tau = 1, df = 3)
#process model at first time step 
cell[1] <- nearest(mu[1,1], mu[1,2], S_x[1:SS], S_y[1:SS]) #nearest neighbour in S to mu
mu[1,1] <- expit(beta1*x1[cell[1]] )
mu[1,2] <- expit(beta1*x1[cell[1]] )
#first time step observation model - mu is latent variable
s_lon[1] ~ dt(mu = mu[1, 1], sigma = psi_lon*sigma_lon[1], df = nu_lon[1]) 
s_lat[1] ~ dt(mu = mu[1, 2], sigma = psi_lat*sigma_lat[1], df = nu_lat[1]) 
#process model for each subsequent time step
for (t in 2:TT){ 
cell[t] <- nearest(mu[t,1], mu[t,2], S_x[1:SS], S_y[1:SS]) #nearest neighbour in S to mu[t]
mu[t,1] <- expit(beta1*x1[cell[t]] )
mu[t,2] <- expit(beta1*x1[cell[t]] )
#observation model - mu is latent variable
s_lon[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 1], sigma = psi_lon*sigma_lon[t], df = nu_lon[t])
s_lat[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 2], sigma = psi_lat*sigma_lat[t], df = nu_lat[t]) 
} #t time step
}) #end

#data
data <- list(
s_lon = c(-204193.6, -202193.6, -200193.6),
s_lat = c(2398461, 2398461, 2398461),
sigma_lat = c(0.004142703,0.027369282,0.004594551), 
sigma_lon = c(0.008117727,0.037842190,0.004565261),
nu_lat = c(3.896554,3.000010,3.000010),
nu_lon = c(3.00001,3.00001,3.00001),
S_x = c(-208193.6,-206193.6,-204193.6,-202193.6,-200193.6,-198193.6,-196193.6,-194193.6,-192193.6,-190193.6),
S_y = c(2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461,2398461),
x1 = c(-0.1942948,-0.1942948,-0.1684170,-0.1684170,-0.1942948,-0.2201726,-0.2201726,-0.2460504,-0.2128746,-0.2460504)
)

constants <- list(
TT = 3,
SS = 10
)

inits <- list(sigma_lat=2300,
sigma_lon=2300,
nu_lat=16,
nu_lon=16,
beta1=0,
beta2=-2.1,
beta3=-0.8,
cell=2000)



# build model
habModel <- nimbleModel(postModelCode, data = data, constants = constants, inits = inits, check = FALSE)

Thanks for any thoughts!

Cheers,
Rowenna

messages.subject: Re: Graph contains a cycle - using latent to select covariate value?
parts:
I am taking a bit of a stab in the dark without fully grasping your model, but if it has temporal dynamics, should there be a time-lag somewhere?

For example, should it be
mu[t,1] <- expit(beta1*x1[cell[t-1]] )

-Perry

parts:
Hi Perry,

Thanks again for the quick reply. I think you are right but interestingly it's not how the model is written in the paper I'm looking at but a time lag is coded in their sampler. 

Just for some background - it's a state-space resource selection function. The observation model accounts for the error around my observation data. I also really parred back the rsf for the example but maybe too much!

Cheers,
Rowenna
